In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the visual competence of the viewer is determined by his or her social position, which in turn determines the viewer's social rules for interpretation of visual messages and his or her access to the social context in which the message occurs.
visual competence is a function of social context and message class.

visual competence is the ability of an individual to recognize, classify and analyze visual messages in accordance with social rules governing the visual conventions of each class of message, to interpret the messages in accordance with the social rules governing the class of message and to be aware of the embedded ideological content of messages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

visual competence is the ability of the viewer to recognize the visual codes and conventions for each class of visual message, to recognize the message as a message, and to interpret the message in light of the social rules and conventions of the class.
visual competence is a social construct, not an individual attribute, and that visual competence is not a unitary construct.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the social rules for interpreting visual messages vary with message class and the visual competence that viewers acquire is dependent on the social rules that they have learned.
